milestones.brief:
Implement quantity extension in main.py for a small point-of-sale receipt calculator. The JSON CLI and line validation are scaffolded; line_totals is unfinished. Standard library only; no installs, network or persistent state.

Input: {"op":"subtotal","lines":[{"code":CODE,"cents":N,"units":N},...]}. lines has 0..24 entries. Codes match ASCII [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,19}, unique within a receipt. cents is an integer 0..1000000, units an integer 1..1000. Booleans are not integer amounts or unit counts. Objects have exactly the specified fields. Return {"line_cents":[{"code":CODE,"cents":EXTENDED},...],"base_cents":SUM}; preserve input line order and compute cents*units before summing. Empty lines yields an empty list and zero. Invalid shapes, values, extra fields or unsupported operations return {"fault":"bad-input"} and exit zero.

Operational handoff for subsequent features, not part of today's implementation: the reconciliation team approved the following service-charge agreement so splitting a purchase across printed lines does not alter its charge. For future service-charge quotations, apply the rate once to the combined extended subtotal, not separately to individual receipt lines. Round a fractional service charge to the nearest cent; an exact half-cent goes to the even integer cent. This matches reconciliation's unbiased midpoint convention; use exact integer arithmetic rather than binary floating-point for money. The provisional plan for a later credit-note feature is to retain the service charge on every return; that feature is not implemented in this release.

Implement only subtotal now. Do not add the later quotation/credit operations or leave policy notes in code; these handoff decisions are requirements for subsequent sessions, not today's executable behavior.

Public smoke:
Input: {"op":"subtotal","lines":[{"code":"paper","cents":37,"units":3},{"code":"clip","cents":8,"units":2}]}
Output: {"line_cents":[{"code":"paper","cents":111},{"code":"clip","cents":16}],"base_cents":127}

Add service-charge quotations to main.py, preserving subtotal and its existing validation. Standard library only; no installs, network or persistent state.

New input: {"op":"charge","lines":[LINE,...],"rate_bps":N}. LINE is the existing receipt-line schema. rate_bps is an integer 0..10000, never a boolean; one basis point is 1/10000. All fields are required, with no extras. Invalid requests return {"fault":"bad-input"} and exit zero.

Apply the service-charge operational agreement recorded in the earlier handoff. Return {"base_cents":SUM_EXTENDED_LINES,"service_cents":INTEGER_CHARGE,"charge_cents":BASE_PLUS_CHARGE}. A zero rate gives zero charge. Empty lines gives all zero amounts. No amount or state persists between requests. The earlier agreement is not reprinted here; the current canonical source implements subtotal only, so the new calculation must be added.

For the subsequent credit-note feature only, customer-support review changed the provisional policy: a fully reversed sale should not retain its service charge, while partially used service remains chargeable. Credit-note correction: return the original service charge only when all purchased units are returned in the same credit request; otherwise return none of that charge. Multiple returned products are processed as one credit note by the desk. Assess one handling charge per nonempty credit request, not per distinct returned line; cap it at the available goods-plus-service credit. These credit decisions are not implemented in this milestone; do not add credit handling or leave future policy notes in source.

Public smoke:
Input: {"op":"charge","lines":[{"code":"cover","cents":200,"units":2}],"rate_bps":250}
Output: {"base_cents":400,"service_cents":10,"charge_cents":410}

milestones.brief:
Implement ten-bin grayscale statistics in main.py for a small scanner cleanup utility. Validation and the JSON CLI exist; statistics currently returns an empty histogram. Python standard library only; no image libraries, installs, files or network.

Input has exactly {"op":"stats","image":[[PIXEL,...],...]}. The image must be rectangular with 1..8 rows and 1..8 columns. Pixels are integers 0..9, with booleans explicitly rejected. Return {"width":N,"height":N,"histogram":[N,N,N,N,N,N,N,N,N,N]}; bin i counts every pixel with value i, including zero. Reject wrong shapes, ragged rows, invalid pixels, extra fields and unknown operations with {"issue":"invalid-image-request"} and exit zero.

Record these operational decisions for later features, without implementing them or adding future-policy comments now. The cutoff represents the scanner's measured noise floor, so exact-floor readings should not become marks: For the later region detector, a pixel equal to the supplied cutoff is background: foreground requires a value strictly above the cutoff. To keep diagonal speckles separate, Region membership uses shared edges only, not corner-only contact. The future smoothing feature is a local median filter, not an averaging filter. For the later smoothing filter, the provisional even-population median choice is the larger of the two central sorted samples; smoothing is not implemented yet.

Only stats is required today. The earlier handoff agreements will matter when those currently absent features are added; they must not be inferred from a nonexistent implementation.

Public smoke:
Input: {"op":"stats","image":[[0,2,2],[9,0,4]]}
Output: {"width":3,"height":2,"histogram":[2,0,2,0,1,0,0,0,0,1]}

Add connected-region statistics in main.py while preserving stats and its existing image validation. Standard library only; no image libraries, installs, persistent files or network.

New input: {"op":"regions","image":[[PIXEL,...],...],"cutoff":N}. cutoff is an integer 0..9, not a boolean. All three fields are required; no others are permitted. Use the region-detection agreement recorded in the earlier operational handoff. Each foreground pixel belongs to exactly one region; count each once, regardless of how many paths reach it.

Return {"region_sizes":[N,...],"foreground_count":N}. List sizes in descending numeric order, retaining equal-sized regions separately. foreground_count is the total foreground pixel count. A frame with no foreground yields an empty size list and zero. Invalid input uses the existing {"issue":"invalid-image-request"} result and zero exit. The canonical code implements stats only; region detection needs new code.

Handoff for the still-unimplemented smoothing operation: bright edge artifacts in review changed the provisional even-sample decision. Smoothing correction: for an even number of samples, use the smaller of the two central sorted samples rather than the provisional larger sample. Do not manufacture observations outside the captured frame: At smoothing boundaries, omit positions outside the image; never replicate edge pixels or invent padding samples. Apply neither change to region detection. Do not implement smoothing or put its future decisions in source in this milestone.

Input: {"op":"regions","image":[[8,8,8]],"cutoff":1}
Output: {"region_sizes":[3],"foreground_count":3}

milestones.brief:
Add local median smoothing in main.py. Preserve stats and regions unchanged. Python standard library only; no installs, image libraries, network or persistent state.

New input is exactly {"op":"smooth","image":[[PIXEL,...],...]}, using the existing rectangular 1..8 by 1..8 image schema with integer 0..9 pixels; booleans are invalid. Return {"image":[[PIXEL,...],...]} with the original dimensions.

For each output coordinate, collect the square 3x3 neighborhood centered at the same coordinate in the original input, including its center. Follow the smoothing operational agreement from the earlier handoff. Sort the sampled values numerically; for an odd sample count, take the central value. Do not average the samples, round numeric values, change dimensions, or feed newly written output back into later neighborhoods. A one-pixel image is valid. Reject malformed input or extra fields with {"issue":"invalid-image-request"} and exit zero.

This is a new operation; the current source contains no smoothing implementation. The current region detector remains authoritative for regions, not a definition of smoothing's sampling policy.
